The surrounding ST4 and ST7 pairs fall by about 0.35–0.39 bar; farther P6 stations show smaller falls of about 0.11–0.20 bar. Nearby connected P3 stations ST7–ST8 fall only 0.05–0.09 bar. The changes develop around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording and persist to its 150-second end; the numerical screening records at least 54 seconds of persistence across four P6 stations and two shared-data connection groups. These are before/after changes within the recording, not measured departures from a supplied normal-pressure reference.

Why this matters
The P6 pattern spans both gateways, the shared data connections serving its sensors, and is strongest at adjacent stations rather than every other station. That supports checking a physical pressure event first, but agreement does not prove independent measurements or a leak. P2 comparison sensors instead rise by about 0.38–0.43 bar and move back toward their earlier pressure in the final six seconds. Operating records were not supplied, so a valve, compressor or pressure-setting change remains untested.

Other instruments to check
Treat P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B as suspect measurement paths: they abruptly fall together by about 0.76–0.83 bar on gateway-P7-0, while the intervening stations on gateway-P7-1 change much less. This is not a confirmed hardware fault. Brief spikes are flagged on P6-ST1-A, P6-ST2-B, P6-ST3-A, P6-ST3-B, P6-ST7-B, P6-ST8-A and P6-ST8-B; the surrounding joint pressure pattern means those flags alone do not establish unreliable sensors. Overall usable-sample coverage is 100%, but the health review is partial and completeness does not establish accuracy.

What would resolve the remaining question
Request engineer comparison with independent P6 pressure and flow measurements, incident-time operating records, and the P7 gateway/calibration register. These checks would distinguish a physical pressure change from operating effects or shared measurement bias. This applies KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-QUALITY-R1, KN-OPERATING-R1 and KN-LOCALIZATION-R1 to the observed comparisons, without converting screening into causal certainty.

competing_causes.text: P6 has a sustained pressure fall strongest at adjacent stations ST5–ST6, with smaller falls at surrounding stations and the connected P3 comparison locations. Agreement across two gateways makes an isolated single-sensor explanation less persuasive and supports prioritizing this region for engineer review. However, simultaneous measurements are not proof of independence, and neither pressure magnitude nor the screening label establishes a physical leak. Independent pressure and flow checks, together with operating context, are needed before attributing the pattern or qualifying a location.

P7's paired sensors at every other station show similar abrupt negative shifts on gateway-P7-0, while intervening stations on gateway-P7-1 remain much quieter. This concrete connection-aligned contrast supports investigating the shared measurement path, rather than declaring all pressure anomalies sensor faults. The affected P7 signals also correlate with P6's change, so a concurrent physical or operating event cannot be excluded. Confirm gateway assignments and compare raw readings with an independent reference; the present evidence identifies suspect observations, not a confirmed hardware failure.

P2-ST1-A and P2-ST8-B rise together by approximately 0.38–0.43 bar while P6 falls, then move toward their earlier pressures near the recording's end. This contrasting sign and recovery justify checking whether an operating change affected the network, but no reviewed valve or compressor records establish such an action. An explanation for P2 would not automatically account for P6's concentrated negative pattern or P7's gateway-aligned shifts. Incident-time records must be compared with the measured timing and affected pipes before accepting an operating explanation.

regional_assessments.text: On P6, ST5–ST6 paired readings fall about 1.38–1.39 bar, compared with 0.35–0.39 bar at ST4/ST7, 0.16–0.20 bar at ST3/ST8 and 0.05–0.09 bar at nearby connected P3 ST7/ST8. The central pairs move closely together, and the pattern spans both P6 gateways rather than following one shared connection. These within-recording changes support a physical-event review priority but are not normal-reference deficits or proof of a leak. Operating records and independent pressure/flow measurements remain necessary, and no qualified inspection interval can be supplied.

P7 ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 pairs show abrupt, sustained falls of approximately 0.76–0.83 bar around the 90-second split; all share gateway-P7-0. Intervening ST2/ST4/ST6/ST8 pairs on gateway-P7-1 change by only about -0.08 to +0.003 bar, making the connection-aligned contrast a concrete reason to review the first group's measurement path. Agreement between two sensors at the same station does not eliminate a shared error, although their correlation with P6 leaves concurrent process effects possible. No missing or invalid received readings appear in this comparison, and no drift or hardware fault is established. Verify the connection register and compare an independent reference before judging these readings reliable.

The reviewed P2 locations rise by 0.3834 and 0.4252 bar, contrasting with the approximately 1.39-bar falls at the compared P6 locations. Their profiles move back toward the earlier reference in the final 144–150-second period, while P5-ST8-A/B show much smaller typical increases of approximately 0.02 bar. This supports checking an operating transient as a competing explanation, not claiming a network-wide operation or treating P5 as evidence of clearance. Only the named comparison instruments were assessed here, and no executed-operation records were reviewed. An engineer should compare incident-time valve, compressor and pressure-setting records with each pipe's sign, timing and recovery.

follow_up_questions: Do independent pressure and flow measurements confirm the sustained P6 ST5–ST6 drop relative to ST4/ST7?
Do the instrumentation register and raw data confirm a shared measurement-path change for P7 ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 on gateway-P7-0?
Were any valve, compressor or pressure-setting changes executed around 90 seconds elapsed, and do they explain P6's fall and P2's rise?

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.

payload.purpose: assess_event_and_location
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

payload.text:
Recommended next step
Prioritize the integrity engineer's review of pipeline P6 around stations ST5 and ST6, with ST4 and ST7 as surrounding comparison stations. This is the strongest connected pressure-drop pattern in the reviewed comparisons, rather than an isolated instrument alert. A leak remains a credible explanation, while a separate measurement-path issue deserves review on P7. No qualified inspection interval is available: these station names identify a review priority, not a leak point or an authorized inspection boundary.

What the readings show
On P6, both sensors at ST5 and ST6 show typical pressure falling by about 1.38–1.39 bar, where bar is a pressure unit. The surrounding ST4 and ST7 pairs fall by about 0.35–0.39 bar; farther P6 stations show smaller falls of about 0.11–0.20 bar. Nearby connected P3 stations ST7–ST8 fall only 0.05–0.09 bar. The changes develop around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording and persist to its 150-second end; the numerical screening records at least 54 seconds of persistence across four P6 stations and two shared-data connection groups. These are before/after changes within the recording, not measured departures from a supplied normal-pressure reference.

Why this matters
The P6 pattern spans both gateways, the shared data connections serving its sensors, and is strongest at adjacent stations rather than every other station. That supports checking a physical pressure event first, but agreement does not prove independent measurements or a leak. P2 comparison sensors instead rise by about 0.38–0.43 bar and move back toward their earlier pressure in the final six seconds. Operating records were not supplied, so a valve, compressor or pressure-setting change remains untested.

Other instruments to check
Treat P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B as suspect measurement paths: they abruptly fall together by about 0.76–0.83 bar on gateway-P7-0, while the intervening stations on gateway-P7-1 change much less. This is not a confirmed hardware fault. Brief spikes are flagged on P6-ST1-A, P6-ST2-B, P6-ST3-A, P6-ST3-B, P6-ST7-B, P6-ST8-A and P6-ST8-B; the surrounding joint pressure pattern means those flags alone do not establish unreliable sensors. Overall usable-sample coverage is 100%, but the health review is partial and completeness does not establish accuracy.

What would resolve the remaining question
Request engineer comparison with independent P6 pressure and flow measurements, incident-time operating records, and the P7 gateway/calibration register. These checks would distinguish a physical pressure change from operating effects or shared measurement bias. This applies KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-QUALITY-R1, KN-OPERATING-R1 and KN-LOCALIZATION-R1 to the observed comparisons, without converting screening into causal certainty.

answer.text:
Recommended next step
Prioritize the integrity engineer's review of pipeline P6 around stations ST5 and ST6, with ST4 and ST7 as surrounding comparison stations. This is the strongest connected pressure-drop pattern in the reviewed comparisons, rather than an isolated instrument alert. A leak remains a credible explanation, while a separate measurement-path issue deserves review on P7. No qualified inspection interval is available: these station names identify a review priority, not a leak point or an authorized inspection boundary.

What the readings show
On P6, both sensors at ST5 and ST6 show typical pressure falling by about 1.38–1.39 bar, where bar is a pressure unit. The surrounding ST4 and ST7 pairs fall by about 0.35–0.39 bar; farther P6 stations show smaller falls of about 0.11–0.20 bar. Nearby connected P3 stations ST7–ST8 fall only 0.05–0.09 bar. The changes develop around 90 seconds elapsed in the recording and persist to its 150-second end; the numerical screening records at least 54 seconds of persistence across four P6 stations and two shared-data connection groups. These are before/after changes within the recording, not measured departures from a supplied normal-pressure reference.

Why this matters
The P6 pattern spans both gateways, the shared data connections serving its sensors, and is strongest at adjacent stations rather than every other station. That supports checking a physical pressure event first, but agreement does not prove independent measurements or a leak. P2 comparison sensors instead rise by about 0.38–0.43 bar and move back toward their earlier pressure in the final six seconds. Operating records were not supplied, so a valve, compressor or pressure-setting change remains untested.

Other instruments to check
Treat P7-ST1-A/B, P7-ST3-A/B, P7-ST5-A/B and P7-ST7-A/B as suspect measurement paths: they abruptly fall together by about 0.76–0.83 bar on gateway-P7-0, while the intervening stations on gateway-P7-1 change much less. This is not a confirmed hardware fault. Brief spikes are flagged on P6-ST1-A, P6-ST2-B, P6-ST3-A, P6-ST3-B, P6-ST7-B, P6-ST8-A and P6-ST8-B; the surrounding joint pressure pattern means those flags alone do not establish unreliable sensors. Overall usable-sample coverage is 100%, but the health review is partial and completeness does not establish accuracy.

What would resolve the remaining question
Request engineer comparison with independent P6 pressure and flow measurements, incident-time operating records, and the P7 gateway/calibration register. These checks would distinguish a physical pressure change from operating effects or shared measurement bias. This applies KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1, KN-QUALITY-R1, KN-OPERATING-R1 and KN-LOCALIZATION-R1 to the observed comparisons, without converting screening into causal certainty.

competing_causes.text: P6 has a sustained pressure fall strongest at adjacent stations ST5–ST6, with smaller falls at surrounding stations and the connected P3 comparison locations. Agreement across two gateways makes an isolated single-sensor explanation less persuasive and supports prioritizing this region for engineer review. However, simultaneous measurements are not proof of independence, and neither pressure magnitude nor the screening label establishes a physical leak. Independent pressure and flow checks, together with operating context, are needed before attributing the pattern or qualifying a location.

P7's paired sensors at every other station show similar abrupt negative shifts on gateway-P7-0, while intervening stations on gateway-P7-1 remain much quieter. This concrete connection-aligned contrast supports investigating the shared measurement path, rather than declaring all pressure anomalies sensor faults. The affected P7 signals also correlate with P6's change, so a concurrent physical or operating event cannot be excluded. Confirm gateway assignments and compare raw readings with an independent reference; the present evidence identifies suspect observations, not a confirmed hardware failure.

P2-ST1-A and P2-ST8-B rise together by approximately 0.38–0.43 bar while P6 falls, then move toward their earlier pressures near the recording's end. This contrasting sign and recovery justify checking whether an operating change affected the network, but no reviewed valve or compressor records establish such an action. An explanation for P2 would not automatically account for P6's concentrated negative pattern or P7's gateway-aligned shifts. Incident-time records must be compared with the measured timing and affected pipes before accepting an operating explanation.

The central pairs move closely together, and the pattern spans both P6 gateways rather than following one shared connection. These within-recording changes support a physical-event review priority but are not normal-reference deficits or proof of a leak. Operating records and independent pressure/flow measurements remain necessary, and no qualified inspection interval can be supplied.

P7 ST1/ST3/ST5/ST7 pairs show abrupt, sustained falls of approximately 0.76–0.83 bar around the 90-second split; all share gateway-P7-0. Intervening ST2/ST4/ST6/ST8 pairs on gateway-P7-1 change by only about -0.08 to +0.003 bar, making the connection-aligned contrast a concrete reason to review the first group's measurement path. No missing or invalid received readings appear in this comparison, and no drift or hardware fault is established. Verify the connection register and compare an independent reference before judging these readings reliable.

The reviewed P2 locations rise by 0.3834 and 0.4252 bar, contrasting with the approximately 1.39-bar falls at the compared P6 locations. Their profiles move back toward the earlier reference in the final 144–150-second period, while P5-ST8-A/B show much smaller typical increases of approximately 0.02 bar. cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.

cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.

cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.

Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.

payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.

cases.name: Leak look-alike: shared connection, operating shift and sensor faults at 60 s
Leak look-alike: shared connection, operating shift and sensor faults at 150 s
cases.answer:
ENGINEER QUESTION
Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING ASSESSMENT
Recommended next step
Focus the integrity engineer's initial evidence review on pipe P7 at stations ST1, ST3, ST5 and ST7. Both sensors at each station remained flagged throughout the reviewed 60 seconds, with no reported spikes, drift or disagreement between the two sensors at the same station. This persistent pattern warrants review before attributing everything to isolated reading problems. A qualified physical inspection interval is withheld because the diagnosis lacked sufficient independent evidence for localization. A leak remains a competing explanation, not a finding. [claim-096, claim-097, claim-100, claim-101, claim-104, claim-105, claim-108, claim-109; KN-LOCALIZATION-R1]

What the readings show
During elapsed seconds 90-150 of the monitored recording, typical pressures at those P7 stations increased only 0.0083-0.0460 bar; bar is a pressure unit. Intervening stations increased 0.0012-0.0557 bar, so these within-window changes do not distinguish the groups. The flagged stations share gateway-P7-0, their data connection; intervening stations use gateway-P7-1. That alignment warrants checking measurement independence, not declaring a faulty gateway. No normal-reference pressure summaries were supplied, so pressure deficits from normal and the anomaly's onset cannot be quantified. Small within-window changes do not establish normal pressure. [subsea_2ae6eeb778624b55aad3d2ee44af7984; KN-INDEPENDENCE-R1]

Why this matters
Pipe P2 shows a separate joint change: both sensors at ST1, ST2, ST7 and ST8 fell during elapsed seconds 146-150, approximately 0.36-0.41 bar below their own earlier recording reference. These stations span two data connections. Compared P7 stations, P6-ST7-A, P6-ST8-A and the P1-ST1 pair did not show that same final-period fall. Review P2's synchronized pressure, flow and operating records separately rather than assuming one explanation covers both pipes. payload.purpose: answer_incident_question
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. payload.purpose: assess_sensor_health
payload.question: Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.
verification_steps: Compare suspect instruments with independent observers and their actual received coverage.
Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration

sources.boundary: Strong, possible, lower-threshold and noisy detections motivate multiscale inspection; not calibrated gas-pipeline attenuation.
sources.reference: User-provided public defense deck, not redistributed

sources.boundary: Motivates prior knowledge and source-quality review; gateway independence requires site instrumentation verification.

cards.guidance: Inspect groups, not isolated alert flags. For pressure-monitoring investigations, a leak hypothesis should be tested against a sustained connected pattern: disruptive changes near the affected region and weaker, related changes farther along the pipes, including below-threshold observations. Compare synchronized profiles, relative magnitudes, timing, recovery and missingness against independent and contrasting instruments. Attenuation is not necessarily monotonic in real branched gas networks; this is a working hypothesis, not a universal law. Scattered impulses, isolated drift or missing data motivate instrumentation checks but can coexist with a leak. Treat hydraulic connectivity and instrumentation dependency as different relationships. Multiple agreeing instruments sharing a gateway, power supply or calibration path may share an error. Correlation is not independence or a confirmed cause. Shared-failure explanations also need observed evidence; do not declare every sensor on a gateway faulty from metadata alone.
limitations: Confirm A/B gateway assignments against the site instrumentation register.
No validated common-cause reliability model is provided.
cards.applies_when: Several instruments show simultaneous changes, particularly paired taps or instruments sharing infrastructure.
cards.review_basis: Dependency-analysis guidance; confirm the site instrumentation dependencies before applying.
counterexamples: Eight taps on one shared conversion path are not eight independent witnesses.
An operating transient can also produce a coherent pressure pattern; attenuation alone cannot identify a leak.
Independent gateways do not exclude an unrecorded shared power or operating cause.
verification_steps: Compare near, farther and weak/quiet connected observers jointly, not only above-threshold supporters.
Contrast a shared-path instrument with an independent observer; compare profiles, valid-sample overlap and graph distances.
Inspect contradictory or asynchronous changes rather than merging branch-level earliest/latest timings into a common onset.
Open applicable maintenance records and check effective revision and scope.

cards.title: Test operating transients as competing explanations

sources.boundary: Review of pressure methods, operating transients and model assumptions; not a site-specific operating procedure.

cards.guidance: Investigate operating changes rather than equating a pressure anomaly with a leak. Compare the observed sign, timing and affected assets with an approved, incident-time-available record. A proposal is not an executed operation, and a superseded record is not current authority. Read the underlying records referenced by a coverage statement. A plausible explanation for one branch does not automatically explain a different pattern elsewhere. Incomplete logs cannot prove that no operation or leak occurred.
limitations: Temporal association is not a causal intervention.
The cited review includes liquid-pipeline methods; its parameters cannot be transferred directly to subsea gas.
cards.applies_when: Pressure changes could coincide with a valve, compressor, setpoint or calibration activity.
cards.review_basis: Research-grounded guidance; apply the current site operating procedure.
counterexamples: A broad positive operating shift does not by itself explain a separate localized negative region.
A real operating change can coexist with a leak or instrumentation fault.
verification_steps: Search affected and contrasting signal regions, not only the proposed inspection branch.
Open current records and distinguish planned, approved and executed activities.
Compare before/after periods near an observed change; note window censoring and retain missingness.

cards.title: Separate a numerical inspection bracket from physical leak localization

sources.boundary: Explains method-dependent localization assumptions; requires verification of site-specific inspection assumptions.

cards.guidance: Use the qualified numerical tool for chainage and retain its assumptions. This method brackets affected stations against unaffected neighbours; it does not solve a calibrated hydraulic inverse problem. Pressure-wave localization requires justified propagation, timing, flow and pipeline assumptions. Do not infer an exact coordinate, leak size or leak probability from anomaly magnitude or from a research formula without its inputs. Withhold a location when coverage or the single-region assumption is inadequate.
limitations: The source review discusses methods with different fluid and deployment assumptions.
Confirm inspection priorities using independent pressure and flow measurements.
cards.applies_when: An engineer requests a leak location or an inspection recommendation from pressure observations.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived inspection guidance; confirm eligibility and site-specific hydraulic assumptions.
counterexamples: A larger pressure residual is not necessarily the nearest sensor to a leak.
Multiple disjoint pressure regions are not resolved by this single-leak bracket.
verification_steps: Check the numerical tool's eligibility, observer independence and unaffected brackets.
State the interval and distinguish it from a confidence interval or physical leak point.
Request expert-selected independent confirmation; do not clear alarms while waiting for an LLM.

cards.title: Expert-guided differential investigation program

sources.boundary: Architecture, expertise capture and open uncertainty/contradiction challenges; no subsea benchmark.

cards.guidance: Use this natural-language program to guide the existing read-only specialist workflow, not to assert an answer. Preserve competing leak, instrumentation and operating explanations. Select measurements and contextual checks that could distinguish them, including counterevidence. Apply only relevant knowledge, explicitly connect it to observed case evidence, and retain contradictions and missing prerequisites. Domain guidance supplies reasoning, not incident facts or authority to clear the numerical warning.
limitations: Inspired by DANA CAPTURE/APPLY and natural-language programs, not an OpenSSA or DanaOS implementation.
The paper's FinanceBench results do not establish pipeline diagnostic accuracy.
cards.applies_when: An anomaly episode requires a bounded, reviewable leak-versus-instrumentation RCA investigation.
cards.review_basis: DANA-inspired investigation program; apply site-reviewed expertise and operator approval.
counterexamples: Retrieving a relevant document without applying it is not RCA.
A well-cited but consistently wrong explanation is not successful expert reasoning.
verification_steps: Quality: establish what was measured reliably and what remains missing.
Diagnosis: inspect connectivity, independent domains and competing signal regions.
Diagnosis: choose relevant operational records and discriminating comparisons.
Response: explain which guidance was applied, supporting and contradicting case evidence, and remaining gaps.
Critic: check case facts and knowledge citations against their original pinned sources.
Handoff: request qualified engineer verification; unresolved evidence remains unresolved.

cards.title: Distinguish unreliable observations from physical process evidence

sources.boundary: Marine data-quality and anomaly-attribution principles; not validation of gas-pipeline leak classification.

cards.guidance: An unusual reading is not itself a faulty sensor or a physical leak. Separate completeness, currentness, accuracy and provenance. Missing values and invalid sentinels are observation gaps, not measured pressure drops. Inspect persistence and paired disagreement, and seek an independent reference before attributing a hardware fault. A detector's attribution score identifies a contribution, not a physical root cause. Malfunction and a physical event can coexist.
limitations: This is a research-derived heuristic, not a field-approved sensor diagnosis.
No universal threshold or sensor-failure probability is established.
cards.applies_when: Pressure alerts coexist with missing samples, spikes, drift or inconsistent instrument readings.
cards.review_basis: Research-derived guidance; application requires site instrumentation review.
counterexamples: A gap during a real leak does not establish a healthy pipeline.
A genuine process transient can produce a large anomaly score on functioning instruments.

Check calibration, units, clock and maintenance context; preserve unobserved periods.
State which sensor claims were reviewed and which remain unchecked.

cards.title: Check common causes before counting independent corroboration
